description: DoE's authoring gate for a queue-grind profile (DR-queue-grinds-run-on-shared-primitives, canonical bug-blitz C8). Pins the engine's closed vocabularies (claude-klabauter's coordinator_core/contract/grind_vocab.py, emitted as grind-vocab.json) as enum $defs so a profile authored against this schema cannot drift from what the engine's own validate_graph will accept. The engine does not read this file — it is DoE's own authoring-time gate, and the pinned $defs are what make the two agree by construction. This schema does NOT re-derive validate_graph's structural graph-shape floor (refute-close before any close, verify downstream of the last fix, totality, acyclicity, per-stage-kind outcome typing, on_fail requirement) — that is the engine's job at emit. There is no 'name' key: the profile's name is its file stem (load_profile(name, profile_dir)). No field anywhere accepts a command-line-shaped string (DR-queue-grinds-run-on-shared-primitives § Negative spec: 'No profile field accepts a command line. Every executable step is a named engine op.') — every executable step is one of the pinned op enums below.

row_id_key.description: The queue row field that names a row's identity for the ledger and receipts.

batch_key.description: Ordered coalesce list of queue row fields a batch is keyed by: the first present, non-sentinel value wins; a row with none batches under `@unkeyed`.

priority.description: The queue row field the selector sorts by, and its direction.

verdicts.description: The profile's own closed triage-verdict vocabulary — checked against the profile, not fixed by the engine (triage's single STAGE_OUTCOMES member is 'profile-declared').

graph.description: Map of stage name to stage node. Edge totality, acyclicity and per-stage-kind outcome typing are validate_graph's job at emit, not this schema's.

status_field.description: The queue row field the closer writes the closed status into.

closed_values.description: Closed status value keyed by the closing branch — lessons close differently per branch.

stamp_fields.description: Queue row field names the closer stamps on close. A field named `closed_by` takes the settling commit; every other field takes the run stamp. The engine fixes those two sources; the profile names only the fields.

absent_sentinels.description: Optional per-field sentinel values the selector's 'absent' operator treats as absence.

triage_policy.description: The operative triage policy, inline in the profile as one text block (a YAML block scalar). The engine hashes it into the receipt's profile digest, so a policy edit is visible on resume. Never a pointer to prose held elsewhere (DR-queue-grinds-run-on-shared-primitives § Alternatives Considered).

appetite.description: Map of appetite preset name to its resolved knob values.

archive_path.description: Directory a closed row's queue file is moved under.

schema.description: The queue row's own schema reference.

args.description: Keyword arguments passed to the source op at emit (e.g. lessons.extract's lessons_path). Values are data, never a command line.

source.description: Optional source stage: one of the closed source ops, with optional keyword args for it. Absent for a profile whose rows are queue-native.

hand_back_types.description: Optional hand-back types this profile adds to the universal set (DR-404 § 3: profiles add, never remove). Kebab-case, unique, disjoint from the universal set; the engine also refuses a type that names a graph node (hand_back_type_collision). An edge target or on_fail may name any graph node, universal hand-back type, or one of these.

edges.description: Map of outcome to the downstream stage name. Per-stage-kind outcome typing and one-edge-per-outcome totality are validate_graph's job at emit.

on_fail.description: The stage's failure path: another graph node (the one permitted back-edge, bounded by the engine to one traversal per path), or a universal or profile-declared hand-back type, which ends the path without spending a retry.

verify.description: Present only on a verify-mode stage: a map of verify key (e.g. 'default', a severity value) to either a bare verify_mode string or {mode: 'op', op: <verify_op>}. A 'default' entry is required — enforced by the engine's validate_graph, not restated here.

where.description: DNF: an array of AND-clauses, each an array of [field, operator, value?] triples. `value` is required for a binary operator (==, in, contains) and absent for a unary one (absent, present).

queue_grind_appetite_preset_knobs.description: concurrency, extra_verification, batch_size, triage_depth, window and max_agent_calls are required on every preset (the engine's own _REQUIRED_KNOBS -- it has no defaults). batch_size/triage_depth are either a bare value or a map keyed by severity/whatever the profile's own vocabulary is (plus an optional 'default' entry). Only where, limit and budget_tokens are overridable at run time (resolve_appetite); the rest are fixed per preset.

x-bump-note: 2.0.0 -> 2.0.1 ZERO SHAPE EFFECT: namespaces this schema's local $defs with a `queue_grind_` prefix (stage_kind, verify_mode, source_op, verify_op, regenerate_op, knob, triage_depth, universal_hand_back_type, where_operator, reserved_key, graph_node, appetite_preset_knobs) so the artifact-shape-contract bundle's flat $defs-hoist does not collide with a later schema declaring the same generic local name. Every $ref within this schema is updated to match; validation is unchanged. 2.0.1 -> 2.1.0 added the optional top-level `hand_back_types` array (DR-404 § 3: profiles add, never remove from the universal hand-back set). 2.1.0 -> 3.0.0 made `source.op` required on the optional `source` stage object (a `source` block with no `op` was accepted before and is rejected now -- MAJOR because a previously-valid `source: {args: {...}}`-shaped document now fails). 3.0.0 -> 4.0.0 (MAJOR, narrowing): each `appetite.*.where` DNF clause is constrained to a `[field, queue_grind_where_operator, value?]` tuple (a malformed clause failed only at the engine before); preset keys are constrained to `queue_grind_knob` via propertyNames; the unreferenced `queue_grind_regenerate_op` pin is removed, since no profile field names a regenerate op. Every shipped profile already conforms.
